The '''1980–81 season''' is '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|79th season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|50th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football. As of 2024, this was the last time Real Madrid had lost a [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup/UEFA Champions League]] final as they have gone on to win all 9 finals since [[1998 UEFA Champions League final|1998]] and avenging their defeat to Liverpool both times in [[2018 UEFA Champions League final|2018]] and [[2022 UEFA Champions League final|2022]]. 

==Summary==
Financial worries did hit [[Luis de Carlos]] Presidency during summer as a result there had not high-profile transfers in,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1980/10/07/deportes/339721213_850215.html|work=El País|title=Points, Wallet and Boots|date=6 October 1980|accessdate=2 July 2020|language=Spanish}}</ref> so, the new arrivals were midfielder [[Ricardo Gallego]] (replacing forward [[Laurie Cunningham]] injured since November and with physical issues until season finale)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1981/03/15/deportes/353458808_850215.html|title=Another surgery for Cunningham again|work=El País|date=14 March 1981|accessdate=2 July 2020}}</ref> goalkeeper Agustín come from its Youth team [[Real Madrid Castilla|Castilla]] and ended loans like [[Rafael García Cortés]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elperiodicodearagon.com/noticias/deportes/garcia-cortes-fichaje-medianoche_1334370.html|work=El Periódico|title=García Cortés A Midnight Transfer|language=Spanish|accessdate=2 July 2020}}</ref> In League the squad was struggling in the middle of the table almost the entire campaign behind local rivals [[Atlético Madrid]] until colchoneros collapsed in the final rounds of the tournament and [[Real Sociedad]] grabbed the first spot tied in points with [[Real Madrid]] but the head-to head matches<ref>RMA 1–0 RSC, RSC 3–1 RMA</ref> was in favor of basque side winning its first title ever.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2016/04/26/mas_futbol/1461658343_691247.html|publisher=as.com|title=Zamora's Goal gives Title to Real Sociedad|accessdate=2 April 2020|date=26 April 2016|language=Spanish}}</ref> In [[1980–81 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] the club was eliminated in Quarterfinals by [[Sporting Gijón]] with an 3–4 aggregate score.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2011/12/03/mas_futbol/1322897233_850215.html|title=El Molinon always gave war to Real Madrid|publisher=as.com|accessdate=2 July 2020|date=2 August 2011}}</ref>

The season is best remembered due to the club's journey around the [[1980–81 European Cup|European Cup]] defeating Irish side Limerick in First Round, in Eightfinals won 3–0 against [[Budapest Honved]], advancing 2–0 against Soviet side [[FC Spartak Moscow|Spartak Moscow]] in Quarterfinals and won the series 2–1 in semi-finals against Italian Champion [[Inter Milan|F.C. Internazionale Milano]] reaching its first Final of the tournament after 15 years. Before the final, President Luis de Carlos reached an agreement with a German supplier being the first time ever the club play with a branded shirt openly.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://as.com/futbol/2020/05/27/primera/1590591915_461944.html|title=The day Real Madrid left the all-white t-shirt|publisher=as.com|language=Spanish|date=20 May 2020}}</ref> However, with Stielike and Cunningham having physical issues the squad lost 0–1 the [[1981 European Cup Final|Final]] against then-heavily favourites English side [[Liverpool F.C.]] recent back-to-back champions in 1977 and 1978.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://icliverpool.icnetwork.co.uk/0500liverpoolfc/europeancup/tm_headline=decimated-liverpool-dig-deep-to-score-famous-win%26method=full%26objectid=15547871%26siteid=50061-name_page.html|title=Decimated Liverpool dig deep to score famous win|work=Liverpool Daily Post|author=Nick Hilton|date=22 April 1981|accessdate=18 September 2011}}</ref>

According to [[Léo Júnior|Junior]] the club made him an offer after the [[1980 World Champions' Gold Cup]] rejected by the Brazilian left-back Defender.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FiwvjQIDmRsC&dq=leovegildo+junior+estilo+de+jogo&pg=PA26 |publisher=Placar Magazine|date= 16 March 1984|accessdate= 20 November 2023|language=Portuguese|title=Flamengo Until Death}}</ref>
